question: How did life first arise on Earth?
description: No proposed pathway yet explains the full transition from prebiotic chemistry to the first self-sustaining organisms.

question: What selective forces caused sexual reproduction to evolve?
description: Sex carries major biological costs, and researchers still debate which evolutionary advantages first outweighed them.

question: How did the first eukaryotic cell originate?
description: The sequence of symbiotic events that joined nuclei, mitochondria, and host cells remains unresolved.

question: How do cells know what size to reach before dividing?
description: Cells coordinate growth and division reliably, but the mechanisms that set their target size are not fully understood.

question: What is dark matter made of?
description: Its gravitational effects are widespread, yet no confirmed particle or alternative explanation accounts for all observations.

question: What drives the accelerating expansion of the universe?
description: Observations imply dark energy, but its physical nature and whether it changes over time remain unknown.

question: Why does the universe contain more matter than antimatter?
description: Known physics does not fully explain how the early universe developed its observed baryon asymmetry.

question: Is the whole universe finite or infinite?
description: Measurements constrain the observable universe, but cannot yet determine the size or topology of everything beyond it.

question: How can quantum mechanics and gravity be unified?
description: Quantum theory and general relativity both succeed in their domains but conflict under extreme conditions.

question: What happens to information when a black hole evaporates?
description: Hawking radiation appears thermal, creating a conflict between black-hole evaporation and quantum information conservation.

question: Is spacetime fundamentally continuous or discrete?
description: Competing approaches to quantum gravity make different claims about spacetime at the Planck scale.

question: How can physics reconcile its two concepts of time?
description: Quantum mechanics treats time as a fixed parameter while relativity makes it part of dynamic spacetime.

question: What neural mechanisms produce subjective experience?
description: Brain activity correlates with awareness, but no account yet explains how it gives rise to lived experience.

question: How does the brain bind separate features into one experience?
description: Color, shape, location, and emotion are processed across neural systems yet arrive as a unified percept.

question: Where are memories stored and how are they retrieved?
description: Multiple brain systems participate in memory, but the precise physical code and retrieval process remain unsettled.

question: What is the biological function of sleep?
description: Sleep is nearly universal and essential, but no single theory explains all of its restorative and adaptive roles.

question: Is the Riemann hypothesis true?
description: The conjectured locations of the zeta function's nontrivial zeros would tightly govern the distribution of prime numbers.

question: Do smooth Navier–Stokes solutions always exist in three dimensions?
description: No proof shows whether ordinary initial conditions can develop singularities in the equations governing fluid flow.

question: Is the Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture true?
description: The conjecture links rational points on elliptic curves to an analytic function, but the general relation is unproved.

question: Which cohomology classes are algebraic, as predicted by the Hodge conjecture?
description: A central bridge between topology and algebraic geometry remains unproved for general projective varieties.

question: Does P equal NP?
description: It is unknown whether every problem whose answer can be checked quickly can also be solved quickly.

source.name: Wikipedia — Unsolved problems in computer science

question: Do one-way functions exist?
description: Modern cryptography assumes functions that are easy to compute but hard to reverse, without a general proof they exist.

source.name: Wikipedia — Unsolved problems in computer science

question: Can graph isomorphism be solved in polynomial time?
description: The best known general algorithms are fast but do not settle whether this foundational comparison problem lies in P.

source.name: Wikipedia — Unsolved problems in computer science

question: Does linear programming have a strongly polynomial algorithm?
description: Existing methods depend on numeric input sizes, and no algorithm is known with a bound based only on dimensions.

source.name: Wikipedia — Unsolved problems in computer science

question: What controls the paths and intensity of storm tracks?
description: Interactions among atmospheric circulation, clouds, and ocean conditions still limit predictive climate models.

question: What determines how many tropical cyclones form?
description: Warm oceans are necessary but do not explain observed storm frequency or how it will respond to climate change.

question: What is Earth's long-term internal heat balance?
description: The planet's cooling history and the distribution of heat-producing elements inside it remain incompletely constrained.

question: What drives equatorial climate oscillations such as ENSO and the QBO?
description: Researchers still debate how stochastic, chaotic, and forced processes combine to produce these major oscillations.

question: Can superconductivity work at room temperature and practical pressure?
description: Known high-temperature superconductors still require extreme conditions, and a practical material has not been demonstrated.

question: How do relativistic effects shape the chemistry of trans-actinide elements?
description: Spin–orbit coupling and electron interactions become extreme in the heaviest elements and remain hard to predict.

question: Can a lithium–air battery become practically useful?
description: Its theoretical energy density is high, but instability, side reactions, and limited cycle life remain unresolved.

question: Why do biomolecules overwhelmingly share one handedness?
description: Life uses strongly preferred molecular chiralities, but their origin and necessity are still disputed.

question: What turns a justified true belief into knowledge?
description: Gettier cases show that truth, belief, and justification can coincide through luck without clearly constituting knowledge.

question: Why is there something rather than nothing?
description: Accounts of particular things do not settle why any universe, law, time, or possibility exists at all.

question: How are mind and body related?
description: Neither dualist nor physicalist accounts have resolved how subjective mental states relate causally to physical processes.

question: How should luck affect moral responsibility?
description: People are judged differently for outcomes and circumstances beyond their control, creating a persistent ethical conflict.

question: What should count as a disease?
description: Physiological dysfunction, suffering, risk, and cultural judgment do not always agree on the boundary of disease.

question: How should population evidence guide treatment for one person?
description: Clinical studies estimate group effects, but translating those averages into reliable individual decisions remains difficult.

question: How can psychiatric diagnoses become more reliable?
description: Independent clinicians often disagree on some diagnoses even when using the same symptom-based manuals.

question: Can mental disorders be classified by their causes?
description: Psychiatric categories remain organized mainly by symptoms because the causal pathways of many disorders are unknown.

question: Why have stocks historically returned so much more than bonds?
description: Standard models struggle to explain the scale of the long-run equity premium using plausible attitudes toward risk.

question: Why do investors value dividend-paying companies differently?
description: No accepted account fully reconciles observed preferences for dividends with theories of equivalent firm value.

question: Can one useful model capture the full range of human economic biases?
description: Behavioral effects are well documented, but no unified model incorporates them while retaining broad predictive power.

question: Does revealed preference really reveal what consumers prefer?
description: Observed choices may not expose a stable ranking when people can afford several options and sequence their consumption.

question: Can an artificial intelligence possess genuine understanding?
description: Fluent behavior can be produced by computation, but whether any system has intentionality or meaning remains contested.

question: How can we distinguish intelligent mimicry from machine sentience?
description: Passing behavioral tests may demonstrate convincing imitation without revealing whether a machine has any inner experience.
